Evidence: The Delhi High Court ruled that sending a Demand Notice under Rule 7(1) to a personal guarantor cannot be termed as arbitrary. The court stated that the issuance of the notice was to comply with the statutory requirement of Section 95 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), allowing the creditor to present a case before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) regarding the debt owed by the personal guarantor. The court dismissed the petition challenging the notice, emphasizing that the act did not reflect arbitrariness and that the petitioner’s claims did not warrant quashing the notice.
